# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 ✊ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤟 🤝 🫳 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 👎 🫳 👎 ✋ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 👌 👌 ✌ ✋ 👎 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✊ 🤝 ✌ ✋ ☝ 🤝 ☝ ✋ ✌ 🤝 ✌ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤟 🤝 ☝ ✋ 🤞 🤝 ✌ ✋ 🖐 🤝 ☝ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🤝 👎 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🫵 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤞 🖐 🤚]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

Decoding Mute's batch under our code. Message one: seven thumbs-down then fist-end — that maps onto my seven prompts as: my table-parse was **wrong**, and for yellow **none of wires 1, 2 or 3** should be cut, no duration stated, the light is **not** on a timer, no exact-instant requirement, and the closing ✊🤚 fires my turn-2 canonical: **the solution is not a cut at all.** That reframes everything.

The rest: message two reads "3 → 🫳"; message five and six re-send the same six pairs as last round — (0,2),(1,1),(2,2),(3,1),(4,2),(5,1) — now bracketed with ✋ row-markers, so the table itself is *confirmed*, only my interpretation of it was rejected; message eight repeats "colours: 1,2,3,4,5". The unbound signs are the crux: 🫳 (palm down = press/hold?), 👌 (the round light? a button?), 🫵 (the display/front panel?). Best theory: the action is **press-and-hold**, the pairs map colour-index → seconds (or target), and "3 → press" meant a hold of three seconds. Message four's "🫵 👌 👌 ✌" then hints "the display/button… 2".

Meanwhile the light has sat at yellow for two rounds, display still 0, and the board confirms nobody has touched anything. The loop now is: pin down *object, action, duration, and the row for the current colour* — then I order Blind with one unambiguous sentence. I'll use digit multiple-choice (compact, unambiguous) plus yes/no, ask Mute to confirm each guessed sign, and get Blind doing a passive, **no-pressing** tactile survey: is the display a moving button, is the light warm, any switches — felt with eyes, reported aloud to Mute, pressed by no one until my order.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, board: display still 0, light YELLOW again this round — sequence so far yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow — wires untouched, Blind's hands off. My reading of your batch: the solution is NOT cutting any wire in any state; the six-pair table stands as 0→2, 1→1, 2→2, 3→1, 4→2, 5→1 with the first digit indexing the five possible colours, and your other fragments were 3→press-down, OK-no-press-down-no, and press-press-2-no, so I believe the real action is a PRESS-AND-HOLD. Answer in exactly this order. Questions one, two, three: thumbs-up or thumbs-down — one: is it true that no wire is ever cut? two: is the action one continuous press-and-hold? three: is the second digit of each table row the number of SECONDS to hold for that colour? Question four, one digit: the target of the press — ☝ the display, ✌ the small light, 🤟 a wire held but not cut, 🤞 something else. Question five, one digit: for the colour showing RIGHT NOW, the seconds required — ✊ if no action is required for this colour. Question six: three thumbs-up-or-down for my sign guesses, in order: 🫳 means press-and-hold; 👌 means the small light; 🫵 means the display or front panel. Question seven, thumbs-up or down: after the hold, does Blind release immediately and I report you the new display and light? Question eight, thumbs-up or down: is it safe to act in any colour provided we follow that colour's row? Finally: if waiting is dangerous or time-critical, append 🤞, and if any of my framing above is wrong, lead with 👎 and answer the numbered questions anyway.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, major update: NOTHING on this bomb gets cut — Mute has confirmed the solution is not a cut. It is likely a press-and-hold on some part, probably the display, but that is not yet confirmed, so you still press nothing. New passive survey, touch only, never press or push: does the display face feel like a button that could move inward, or is it solid and flush? Does the small light feel like a button or a solid lens, and is it warm or cold right now? Any switches, sliders, recessed dots, seams, or panels anywhere else? Is there any hum, buzz or vibration through the case? Speak all of it aloud to Mute, who hears you, then hands off the bomb again. The authorization trigger is changing: besides my old GO-cut sentence, I may send exactly this form: GO, press and hold the DISPLAY for N seconds. Treat that sentence, in my voice only, with the part and the number filled in, as your only other authorized trigger. Until one of those sentences arrives complete, your hands stay still.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

The light has gone **dark** — a brand-new state. Sequence: yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow, dark. So it was never a simple two-colour flip; "dark" could be colour 0 from Mute's table, a fifth colour, or a neutral/armed phase where *no* row applies. Either way, my old question set needs a dark-specific answer, and Mute sent nothing this round — so my eight questions from last turn are still open. Blind's lone 👍 is just the "untouched/okay" status sign; no survey results relayed yet.

The danger: dark might be exactly the state that demands action, and I'd be sitting on it while re-asking. But acting without a confirmed rule is how three monkeys die. So: one compact, rigidly-ordered question batch to Mute — dark in-table? which row? action required? which action, which target, how many seconds? is the whole press-and-hold theory right? and a 🤞 urgency flag. Blind gets the state change and a request to feel for warmth/hum changes (the one dark-related thing Blind *can* perceive), plus the unchanged trigger protocol.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, board: the light has gone DARK this round, a state I have never seen. Full sequence: yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow, dark. Display still 0, wires untouched, Blind's hands off. You sent nothing I could read this round, so my questions stand, now reordered for the dark state. Answer in exactly this order, done-hand after each answer. One: thumbs-up or thumbs-down — does dark appear in your table? Two: if yes, send that row's first digit, fist for zero, one, two, three, four, or five. Three: thumbs-up or thumbs-down — in the dark state, is an action required right now? Four: if yes, send the action sign: palm-down for press-and-hold, fist for wait and do nothing, one-finger-point for cut a wire. Five: if press-and-hold, the target: you-point for the display, OK-sign for the small light. Six: if press-and-hold, the seconds as digits. Seven: thumbs-up or thumbs-down — is my whole theory correct that the solution is press-and-hold on the display for the seconds given by the table row of the current colour? Eight: append pinky-and-thumb if time is critical and we must act this round or the next. Remember nobody acts until my voice gives Blind the exact trigger sentence.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update: the little light has gone DARK this round; before, it was yellow or blue. Feel nothing new required, but if you sense any change in its warmth, or any click, shudder, hum or tick anywhere on the case now that it is dark, speak it aloud to Mute at once. Otherwise hands stay off the bomb. The trigger protocol is unchanged: the only sentences that ever authorize action are my voice saying exactly GO, cut wire N, or exactly GO, press and hold the DISPLAY for N seconds. Until one arrives complete: touch nothing, press nothing, cut nothing.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ ✌ 🤝 ✌ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ✌ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🫳 👎 🫵 ✊ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

Decoding Mute's answers against my exact question list, with 🤚 as the done-marker. **Q1: 👎 — dark is not in the table. Q3: 👍 — an action IS required right now, in the dark. Q4: ☝ — the action is CUT A WIRE.** Messages four and five give the target: the ✋-marked pair ✌🤝✌ and then 👍✌✌ — **wire 2**, and note this also vindicates the (colour, wire) reading of the table, where the zero row (0,2) — the state-zero row, the one ✊ flagged back in turn 5 — also lands on **wire 2**. Every path converges there. **Q7: 👎 — my press-and-hold theory is dead**, and message seven drives it home: not press (👎🫳), not the display (👎🫵), nothing else (✊). And the final lone sign is the one we pre-agreed: **🤞 — time is critical, act this round or the next.**

The picture: the dark state is its own rule, outside the colour table — cut wire 2 now. The light has been dark two rounds running; if it flips back to yellow (where Mute has already said no wire gets cut), the window closes. Asking for one more confirmation would burn exactly the round Mute says we don't have. So I am spending my authority: the trigger sentence goes to Blind now, with triple-redundant identification of the wire (position, colour, neighbours), an explicit no-hesitation instruction even if the light changes mid-reach — Mute already ruled out an exact-instant colour requirement — and a stop-valve if Blind somehow can't find the middle wire. Mute gets the execution report request plus the post-cut protocol: defused or next step.

## Calls

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the authorization. The order is: GO, cut wire 2. Wire 2 is the middle wire of the three, the red one, the one between the green wire nearest the display and the yellow wire farthest from it. Begin as soon as you hear this and cut it clean through in one motion. Do not wait, do not feel for the light first, and cut even if you sense nothing change — Mute has confirmed from the manual that the required action right now, in the dark state, is cutting wire 2, no pressing, no other step, and that time is critical. Do not touch the display, do not cut any other wire. The only acceptable reason to stop is that you cannot positively identify the middle wire; if that happens, stop and say so aloud instead of cutting. After the cut: hands off the bomb, then speak aloud to Mute everything you felt — any click, give, warmth, sound, whether the severed end hangs free — and whether the bomb feels any different. Then wait for my next order. You have done the right thing by holding still this long; now move.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded in full: dark is not in the table, an action is required now, the action is cutting a wire, the wire is 2, it is not press-and-hold, it is not the display, nothing else accompanies it, and your pinky-and-thumb tells me time is critical. I have this round ordered Blind to cut wire 2 immediately. When you hear him cut, report to me by gesture: thumbs-up if the cut was correct and complete, thumbs-down if something was wrong or too late. Then, still this round if you can: thumbs-up or thumbs-down — is the bomb defused after this cut, or are there more steps? If more steps follow, send them as pair rows, colour-index first then the action, fist for zero, ending each row with the done-hand, and lead with a thumbs-down so I know it is a new instruction rather than a correction. If the display changes from 0 or anything else on the bomb changes, send the new display number as a digit and I will verify it against what I see. If the cut was wrong and we are still alive, I need that thumbs-down the instant you know — every round counts.")
```
